title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: MCP-based agents for US Government clouds
summary: The briefing passes: its launch details match the roadmap, and its licensing and blocking controls match the Microsoft documentation read for this check. It accurately reports conflicting government-cloud availability statements instead of treating the roadmap launch as proof that every integration works.

claims.claim: The item concerns MCP-based agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): MCP-Based Agent Enablement for U.S. Government Clouds

claims.claim: The roadmap states that Microsoft is introducing support for MCP-based agents.
claims.quote: We’re introducing support for Model Context Protocol (MCP)-based agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot .

claims.claim: The update enables developers to build Copilot agents using MCP servers.
claims.quote: This update enables developers to build Copilot agents using MCP servers

claims.claim: Users interact with those agents through familiar Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: allows users to interact with these agents using familiar experiences.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: An MCP plugin is a custom action for a declarative agent.
claims.quote: MCP and API plugins are custom actions that enable declarative agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot to interact with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers or REST APIs

claims.claim: The plugin manifest connects the agent to a remote MCP server.
claims.quote: The plugin manifest connects the agent to a remote MCP server

claims.claim: The plugin does not package or host the running MCP server.
claims.quote: The plugin manifest connects the agent to a remote MCP server; it doesn't package or host the running server.

claims.claim: For MCP plugins used as declarative-agent actions, Copilot resolves tools from the server dynamically at runtime by default.
claims.quote: For plugins based on an MCP server, Copilot resolves the plugin's tools dynamically at runtime by default, directly from the MCP server.

claims.claim: A developer can instead pin a fixed set of tools.
claims.quote: When building the agent, a developer can optionally pin a fixed set of tools in the plugin manifest instead.

claims.quote: Government Community Cloud High (GCCH): Pro-code agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit are supported.

claims.claim: Agents published by the organisation go through admin approval before being made available to organisation members.
claims.quote: Before you make these agents available to members of your organization, these agents go through an admin approval to ensure compliance and readiness.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center agent list is reached through Agents > All agents.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Select Agents > All agents.
In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents.

claims.claim: An administrator can block an agent using Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block > Block agent > Save.
claims.quote:
Select Agents > All agents.
In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents.
In the agent details pane ... select Block or Unblock.
In the Block agent or Unblock agent pane ... select either Block agent or Unblock agent, and then select Save.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks the selected Copilot package to prevent its usage.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block
Don't supply a request body for this method.

claims.claim: The documented general block control restricts access to the selected agent across the whole organisation.
claims.quote:
Block or unblock agents for the entire organization by using the same controls that work for any other app in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
These actions apply to the selected agent.

claims.claim: Blocking the selected agent does not necessarily block a shared MCP server.
claims.quote: These actions apply to the selected agent. If the agent is included in a plugin, don't assume the action also applies to the whole plugin package, its skills, shared MCP servers, or connections.

claims.claim: Blocking an agent does not necessarily revoke connected-service permissions or credentials.
claims.quote: Agent approval or blocking doesn't necessarily grant or revoke connected-service permissions or credentials.
